item.title: This Man Bought $3,000 of Pudding for Free Flights
item.description:
He bought 12,150 pudding cups... to fly for free.
In 1999, a California civil engineer named David Phillips noticed that a Healthy Choice promotion gave airline miles for product barcodes, and the cheapest item was pudding at about 25 cents a cup. He spent just over $3,000, had Salvation Army volunteers peel the labels in exchange for the pudding, and walked away with more than 1.2 million miles, lifetime Gold status with American Airlines and a tax write-off of about $800. His story even inspired part of a Hollywood movie.
⚠️ Dramatised: characters and scenes are illustrations. The facts are real.
Sources: • Wikipedia: David Phillips (entrepreneur) • Snopes: Pudding on the Ritz • Futility Closet: The Pudding Guy • Now I Know: Pudding One Over • Chief Marketer: Making Lemons into Lemonade

item.title: Disney Secretly Bought a Swamp Using Fake Names
item.description:
Disney bought a secret swamp using fake names. One fake company was called "M.T. Lott"... say it fast.
Walt Disney wanted a huge new park in Florida, but if sellers heard his name, prices would explode. So his team bought swamp, scrub and cattle land through companies like Reedy Creek Ranch Corporation, for under $200 an acre. They gathered more than 27,000 acres, about twice the size of Manhattan, before a reporter cracked the secret in 1965.
⚠️ Dramatised: characters and scenes are illustrations. The facts are real.
Sources: • The Walt Disney Company: The Origins of Disney Parks Expansion: The Florida Project Press Conference • Orlando Sentinel: Disney World news was the biggest scoop in Sentinel history • MousePlanet: Emily Bavar Spills the Beans • AllEars: How Walt Tricked Florida into Becoming Walt Disney World
